newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea '96 trade deficit seen hitting record high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea '96 trade deficit seen hitting record high.

text.p: South Korea is expected to post a record high trade deficit in 1996 due to low memory chip prices, but the shortfall will shrink next year in line with a global economic recovery, Seoul officials said on Monday.

"This year's shortfall will be much larger than the $7.0 billion projected at the beginning of the year because of a slump in semiconductor exports," said Lee Jae-kil, director-general of the trade ministry's trade division.
The ministry now estimated a customs-cleared trade deficit of about $19 billion for this year, against $10.1 billion in 1995, the previous record deficit.
"But the worst seems to be over. World demand for semiconductors will recover in 1997 along with overall economic recovery," Lee said.
He said the government's drive to improve the nation's industrial competitiveness would also help reduce the deficit.
Plunging international prices for South Korea's major exports slashed corporate margins and dented its economic growth.
The Bank of Korea, the central bank, said last week the gross domestic product (GDP) grew a real 6.4 percent in the third quarter of this year, down sharply from a 9.8 percent rise a year before.
It said GDP growth would be brought down to 6.4 percent for all of 1997 from an estimated growth of 6.9 percent for this year as policy priority would be given to redressing the trade balance.

A sharp cut in semiconductor prices meant a plunge in the value of memory chip exports, which was now estimated at about $18 billion for this year, down sharply from the trade ministry's January projection of $30.7 billion.
The ministry said the unit price for 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell 81.2 percent to $9.50 in November from a year earlier.
Ministry officials said weak chip exports also contributed to widening November's trade deficit to $1.83 billion from a shortfall of $414 million a year earlier.
Exports of semiconductors in the month fell 42.1 percent to $1.41 billion. Total exports excluding semiconductors rose 11.6 percent to $10.09 billion, they said.
The ministry said overall exports on a FOB basis rose only 0.3 percent to $11.49 billion in November, while CIF imports increased 12.2 percent to $13.32 billion.
November exports of oil products and auto parts more then doubled from a year earlier, it said.
The ministry said imports of capital and consumer goods rose year-on-year 23 percent and 17.3 percent, respectively, in November, contributing to overall import rises.
Imports of raw materials in November increased 7.1 percent year-on-year.
The trade deficit in the first 11 months of this year totalled $18.64 billion, up from a $10.01 billion shortfall in the same 1995 period, the ministry said.

Letters of credit received by South Korean exporters during the first 10 months and the first 20 days of November fell 4.1 percent, while issuances of import licences for the same period rose 8.9 percent.
